name: User Overview

componentsReused: StatCard/EmptyState/ErrorState/Skeleton (local compositions, per M02 design notes)
figma.variablesUsed: all colors/typography/radius via existing CSS variables / Tailwind token mapping, no hardcoded hex/px

backend.summary: No schema change. Added lib/dashboard.ts (getDashboardOverview) reading Finding/Flag/ScanRule (global platform state — schema has no per-user ownership on these models) and the signed-in user's own active GithubToken (metadata only, never the encrypted value). Added lib/format-relative-time.ts helper.

frontend.summary: Built missing shared app shell (components/layout/header.tsx, sidebar.tsx) and (protected)/layout.tsx — Figma-designed but never coded despite M00 DONE. Rewrote (protected)/dashboard/page.tsx from stub to full Server Component with Default/Empty/Error states, added dashboard/loading.tsx for the Loading state (Next.js route-level Suspense fallback). Added reusable ui/stat-card.tsx, empty-state.tsx, error-state.tsx, skeleton.tsx, finding-status-badge.tsx. Extended shared Badge with an 'accent' (blue) variant for APPROVED status — additive, no existing usage changed.

integration.summary: Page fetches real data server-side via getDashboardOverview(session.user.id); no mock/fake production data. Scoped down 'Scan frequency' and 'Repositories monitored' rows shown in the Figma mock (no backing model/config exists yet — those are M04/M08 territory) rather than fabricating values; kept 'Active rules' + link to Scan Rules, which is real.

tests.summary: typecheck: clean. lint: clean. vitest: 10/10 passed (added 5 new tests for format-relative-time). next build: succeeds, /dashboard compiles as a dynamic route.

security.summary: getDashboardOverview never selects GithubToken.encrypted; only active/scopes/lastUsedAt/rateLimitRemaining are read. No redacted snippet or raw secret rendered on the overview. Session required to view account status; unauthenticated/failed session treated as a load error, not a crash.

knownIssues: Shared Table component (node 5:69, owned by M00) still lacks a repeatable Row sub-component; dashboard table built as a plain <table> against tokens instead of a shared Table component — recommend M00 owner add one for future modules to reuse.
StatCard/EmptyState/ErrorState remain local compositions, not shared Figma components, consistent with M02 Figma pass notes.
'Scan frequency' and 'Repositories monitored' fields from the Figma mock are intentionally omitted from the real UI — no backing data model exists yet (scan scheduling config is M04/M08 scope).
notes: REMOVED: superseded by the 2026-08-17 scope correction (no end-user accounts, no per-user dashboard). This module was fully implemented (see backend/frontend/integration sections below, retained for history) and then reverted out of the codebase along with the per-user product model — the files under changedFiles (e.g. app/(protected)/dashboard/*, lib/dashboard.ts, lib/format-relative-time.ts) no longer exist on disk. The prior status of CLAIMED with owner=null was a stale, contradictory leftover of that reversal and has been corrected to REMOVED to match M11.
Do not rebuild the User Overview / Dashboard screens. There is no per-user session or per-user data surface in the current product; the only authenticated area is Admin.

Implementation-agent pass (override of prior figma-designer-only claim per orchestration rules). Figma design was already DONE from a prior design-only pass; this pass added backend data layer, app shell, and full frontend implementation, then verified against the existing Figma screens.

Findings/Flags/ScanRule are global platform state per the Prisma schema (no per-user foreign key) — overview shows the same operational data to any signed-in user; only GitHub account/token status is user-scoped.

Lock cleared manually by user-authorized action on 2026-08-17: rescope-agent lock (PID from lockfile) confirmed dead via independent Get-Process check before deletion. state/locks/M02.lock removed, owner/claimedAt reset to null. Module status field left as-is pending follow-up work.
